chemistry_scientist.state_summary: Round 6 reports 525 observed records, 2805 eligible candidates, no pending records and no validation/test truth. Latest feedback resolves m28 tail persistence across loading and rejects transfer of m211's 50/1 loading displacement to 10/1. Large response errors on m13, m128 and m38 coexist with overprediction on m206 and m189. Targeted curve measurements and specific loading contrasts remain useful for overall Row accuracy; retraining improvement is not established.
important_observations: Measured nitrogen contrasts narrow H_N_condition. At m211 10/1, increasing loading from 54.3 to 162.9 mg changes 18.13/30.88 to 15.66/32.11 mL (d119d77f545c029deace, 810b065b0b86ff8c9aae). The interval widens by 3.70 mL without the approximately +20/+22 mL endpoint displacement recorded across those doses at 50/1 (35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4, 0f06772820e6693753e3). For m90 at 10/1, increasing loading from 110.7 to 166.05 mg changes 48.17/107.99 to 41.71/106.06 (96710afeabc594baa359, c76d0420b34df595c0c9). Completion moves slightly earlier, whereas the measured 5/1 dose contrast moved completion later. No common nitrogen loading correction is supported.

Measured m141 at fixed 46 mg progresses 12.49/23.49 → 15.70/29.42 → 38.94/71.06 mL over 1/1, 2/1 and 10/1 (835b5f2641442576de42, 82d7243f61695e1b94cf, 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0). Its historical 10/1 prediction was too early by 16.90/10.22 mL. Steric shielding of 2,6-dimethylpyridine nitrogen is a chemical consideration, but does not establish weak retention under these conditions.

Alcohol transition questions are partly resolved. Measured m119 at 105.8 mg progresses 11.83/19.31 → 20.00/31.61 → 48.00/77.09 over 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1 (25ffcaa2164643e082b9, 17c1bb3be086a2b6ffec, 776ee2c1e85ebde75168); the new interior prediction was relatively close. Measured m205 at 99 mg rises from 18.27/33.28 at 1/1 to 27.63/51.49 at 2/1 (2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8, c973d4c257be9ef08216), rejecting its predicted shallow response. Measured m200 in pure EA is 8.39/17.32 at 64.585 mg (6c022e06f98c0a9771b6), substantially earlier than its matched 1/1 and 2/1 records.

Naphthyl alcohol transfer was too strong. Measured m206 at 150 mg rises from 5.23/18.30 at 1/1 to 24.25/54.11 at 5/1 (a4fc5d66da363324e2bf, cdf40bcb3f4392f8d7d1). The rise is substantial, but the historical 5/1 prediction was too late by 22.20/20.75 mL. This weakens the transferred amplitude, not the existence of solvent response. Comparison with m205 changes side-chain connectivity, ring attachment and loading; m206's existing 50 mg 2/1 measurement is not a matched-dose intermediate.

H_m28_response is locally resolved toward persistent late elution. At 10/1, measured endpoints are 43.63/75.43, 39.13/81.40 and 38.78/80.88 mL at 58.4, 116.8 and 175.2 mg (db7f9ffa50eb931613f6, 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a, 0dccaa29989ef4956786). The lowest dose has a narrower interval; middle and highest completions are descriptively similar. At 175.2 mg, 5/1 measures 10.65/42.39 (050e2fab4b407ea058cb), establishing a large matched 5/1–10/1 rise. Another broad 10/1 loading grid has reduced immediate value.

Acid curvature was previously overextended into interior ratios. Measured m45 at fixed 85 mg gives 6.63/9.00, 12.33/18.47, 18.73/31.98 and 39.58/65.65 mL at 1/1, 5/1, 10/1 and 20/1 (5e2f71c50a4ccaa1b83e, 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6, 9409394cdc0bcfb31fbc, b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1). New interior records were overpredicted after the earlier 20/1 underprediction. Much of the measured rise occurs between 10/1 and 20/1, but this sparse grid does not establish a sharp physical threshold.

Multifunctional ester response remains distinct. Measured m13 at fixed 168.3 mg gives 9.04/18.17, 17.85/43.86 and 36.92/94.21 mL at 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 (2dbfdf9c2d5defd09f7a, 5d530b2f228ed39ff952, ca467c94f14b2219503e). Historical completion error changes from +13.95 to -37.64 mL between 2/1 and 10/1. In contrast, measured m16 changes only from 7.71/10.10 to 8.50/11.27 across 5/1–20/1 (66f42d226a5f7e934a86, 199a9e57ec9b13740002). Measured m76 rises modestly from 4.58/7.29 to 6.38/11.18 across 2/1–20/1 (40964ac3f659274451ef, 3fd8f569aaeff7edebea), exceeding its nearly flat historical prediction. m13 contains two esters and a ketone; a single ester correction is insufficient.

Ordinary carbonyl transfer failures have opposing directions. Measured m38 at 100 mg rises from 9.32/20.87 at 5/1 to 31.48/58.15 at 20/1 (7b341f30a27433562690, 8f9a7ca0380c405ee685), with both weak-eluent endpoints underpredicted by about 18 mL. Measured m128 at 50 mg rises from 12.16/20.42 at 2/1 to 33.49/73.97 at 20/1 (40d5f6dbba8de32e9852, 55200f8e501a16ffa0cf); completion was underpredicted by 37.94 mL. Conversely, m189 changes from 6.87/14.97 to 4.39/23.10 across 2/1–20/1 (f1dafc187f7b1ec15297, fd9cda2d3ab32ea2a360), rejecting a large predicted onset delay.

Conjugated-ketone evidence also separates endpoints. Measured m164 at 5/1 is 6.00/14.38 and was predicted closely (9f450a70d44f4384353f). Chalcone m165 at 20/1 is 6.22/23.00 (a7f8c888870123f3b277), versus 5.52/12.25 at 2/1 (bb18fe197ad7e24c5ed1): onset changes little while completion increases. The two graphs do not share one endpoint slope. Measured haloarene additions m157 and m149 had modest historical errors (8755c59209c36519ca2d, 7ce4a1f0c500c875df7c), reducing the immediate case for extensive heavy-halogen grids.

candidate_scientific_questions.question: Where does m128's completion rise develop? At its measured 50 mg/DCM 300 uL setup, current predictions are 12.75/29.55 mL at 5/1 and 15.69/35.63 at 10/1. An interior anchor distinguishes retention already developed at moderate ratio from a rise nearer 20/1. These are alternative informative conditions, not a proposed batch.
Does m38 interpolate reliably after its large 20/1 transfer failure? The 100 mg, 10/1 candidate predicts 18.18/32.87 mL and preserves the measured 5/1 and 20/1 setup, including the 1000 uL DCM plug.

How much of low-dose m141 retention develops by 5/1? This 46 mg candidate predicts 17.60/42.11 mL. It supplies an interior point on the measured low-dose curve and directly contrasts the observed 138 mg 5/1 condition, addressing curvature and local loading together.

Does an m211 loading displacement begin by 20/1? This 108.6 mg candidate predicts 25.20/42.97 mL and contrasts observed 54.3 mg at that ratio. Its dose differs from the 162.9 mg level used in the established 10/1 and 50/1 contrasts, so it only partially localizes the interaction.

Is m206's early 150 mg 1/1 onset also present at low loading? The 50 mg 1/1 candidate predicts 8.00/20.22 mL. Together with observed 50 mg 2/1 and 150 mg 1/1, it adds a controlled dose contrast and a low-dose solvent slope.

Does m13's acquired response transfer toward stronger eluent or to related acetoacetate connectivity? At 168.3 mg, m13 predicts 11.32/26.36 mL at 1/1, above its measured 2/1 endpoints. Separately, m107 at 5/1 and 54.5 mg predicts 24.24/52.13 and extends its measured same-dose 2/1 setup. These address within-graph shape and transfer between linked methacrylate/acetoacetate and methoxyethyl acetoacetate.

Are elevated pure-EA completions being transferred too broadly? At unchanged setup, m164 predicts 5.44/35.65 mL in pure EA but 6.88/12.18 at 1/1; its measured 2/1 completion is 9.90. m165 predicts 6.39/22.21 in pure EA versus measured 1/1 completion of 10.04. Solvent-strength knowledge makes these prospective maxima discriminating, but measured exceptions elsewhere prevent declaring them wrong.

How does novel phosphorus graph m202 behave? A fixed 61.15 mg/DCM 300 uL pure-EA–5/1 pair predicts approximately 4.13/7.16 → 5.88/16.59 mL. The supplied SMILES has formal positive charge on phosphorus and no counterion. Do not reinterpret it as neutral phosphate or phosphine oxide. Novelty alone does not establish transferable value.

chemistry_scientist.possible_model_blind_spots: Observed feedback requires graph-by-ratio-by-loading responses. m211 changes the kind of dose response with ratio, m90 completion changes dose-response direction, and m28 completion is approximately stable only over part of its dose range. A weak-eluent correction can also overpredict interior conditions, as m45 demonstrates. Current adaptation around m13, m128 and m38 therefore does not establish accuracy of their remaining curves.
chemistry_scientist.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: Assess redundancy using molecule plus all five condition columns. Candidates 62c643c64fefa1a9b0c1 and f106b85660c480a44538 encode the same m76 input; 07a55cdab65b05f31561 repeats the measured m82 154.35 mg, 20/1 input. Replication can resolve a specific ambiguity, but catalog multiplicity does not add chemical coverage. Further broad grids on m28 loading, m82, m27 and previously revised anomalies have reduced immediate value. Ordinary ester, carbonyl, ether and hydrophobic regimes remain relevant alongside polar failures.
warnings: Only observed-table IDs establish measurements; all candidate endpoints above are current predictions. Historical errors are premeasurement prediction minus measurement, not current residuals or unbiased overall Row error estimates.

General chemical knowledge supports silica hydrogen bonding, acid/base interactions and usually stronger elution with more EA. Steric access, enolization, intramolecular hydrogen bonding, dissolution and adsorption-site occupancy remain untested explanations here. HBA counts and TPSA do not establish equal silica interaction.
Use density-derived loading_amount_mg. The higher-dose m120 5/1 record used 111.3 mg; its matched higher-dose 1/1 and 2/1 records used 166.95 mg.
V2 minus V1 is physical elution interval width. Crossed quantiles, including negative V1 width for adbaa4b00d492d64eed5, prevent interpreting reported quantile widths as calibrated uncertainty.

Preserve conflicting m73 records and the slightly reversed m195 measurement a917c928912c74862968. Recurrence of m194 behavior across different conditions does not establish same-input reproducibility.

ml_scientist.state_summary: Seed 6101, free_llm32_dual_expert_v1, round 6: 525 observed records, 2805 declared eligible candidates, no pending records and no validation/test records. Latest measurements partly resolve the nitrogen and m28 loading questions, while m13, m128, m38 and m206 expose different prospective transfer failures. The supplied pool favors targeted tests of graph-dependent solvent curves and separate endpoint responses. Successful recent interpolations weaken the case for continuing every previously difficult local program. The objective remains overall Row V1/V2 accuracy and label efficiency after retraining.
ml_scientist.important_observations:
Measured evidence revises H_N_condition: at m211 10/1, increasing loading from 54.3 to 162.9 mg changes 18.13/30.88 to 15.66/32.11 mL (d119d77f545c029deace, 810b065b0b86ff8c9aae). The -2.47/+1.23 mL changes differ substantially from the approximately +20/+22 mL displacement at 50/1 (35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4, 0f06772820e6693753e3). Thus the 50/1 displacement does not generalize to 10/1. At m90 10/1, 110.7 versus 166.05 mg gives 48.17/107.99 versus 41.71/106.06 (96710afeabc594baa359, c76d0420b34df595c0c9): completion remains descriptively similar despite an onset difference. This does not establish statistical equivalence. Low-dose m141 rises from 12.49/23.49 at 1/1 to 15.70/29.42 at 2/1 and 38.94/71.06 at 10/1 (835b5f2641442576de42, 82d7243f61695e1b94cf, 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0), supporting its own solvent curve.

Measured evidence retains H_OH_condition while rejecting common response amplitudes: m119's matched 2/1 measurement is 20.00/31.61 (17c1bb3be086a2b6ffec), reasonably close to its premeasurement prediction and between its existing anchors. m205 at 99 mg rises from 18.27/33.28 at 1/1 to 27.63/51.49 at 2/1 (2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8, c973d4c257be9ef08216), rejecting the predicted shallow response. m200 in pure EA measures 8.39/17.32 (6c022e06f98c0a9771b6), substantially earlier than its matched 1/1 and 2/1 records. m206 at 150 mg rises from 5.23/18.30 to 24.25/54.11 across 1/1–5/1 (a4fc5d66da363324e2bf, cdf40bcb3f4392f8d7d1). Its predicted 5/1 endpoints were about 22/21 mL too late. Transfer from the severely underpredicted m205 curve therefore overstated m206 retention. New m119 and m200 anchors reduce their immediate continuation value.

Measured evidence locally resolves H_m28_response persistence: at 10/1, 58.4, 116.8 and 175.2 mg measure 43.63/75.43, 39.13/81.40 and 38.78/80.88 (db7f9ffa50eb931613f6, 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a, 0dccaa29989ef4956786). Late elution survives all tested doses. The lowest dose has a narrower physical interval, approximately 31.79 versus 42.1–42.3 mL. At 175.2 mg, changing 5/1 to 10/1 moves endpoints from 10.65/42.39 to 38.78/80.88 (050e2fab4b407ea058cb, 0dccaa29989ef4956786). Loading cannot explain the entire solvent response; further dose-grid expansion has diminished value.

Measured evidence refines H_acid_ester_transfer: fixed-dose m45 measures 6.63/9.00, 12.33/18.47, 18.73/31.98 and 39.58/65.65 at 1/1, 5/1, 10/1 and 20/1 (5e2f71c50a4ccaa1b83e, 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6, 9409394cdc0bcfb31fbc, b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1). Latest interior V2 predictions were 15.28 and 20.23 mL too late after acquisition of the distant endpoint. The acid/ester distinction persists, but the new curve substantially constrains its interior ambiguity. These anchors do not establish a sharp transition.

Measured evidence narrows H_conjugated_curve: m164 at 5/1 measures 6.00/14.38 with premeasurement errors below 0.8 mL (9f450a70d44f4384353f), demonstrating successful local interpolation. Chalcone m165 changes from 5.52/12.25 at 2/1 to 6.22/23.00 at 20/1 (bb18fe197ad7e24c5ed1, a7f8c888870123f3b277). Transfer of m164's onset delay to m165 is weakened: m165 mainly extends completion.

Measured evidence strengthens H_ester_connectivity: m13 at 168.3 mg measures 9.04/18.17, 17.85/43.86 and 36.92/94.21 at 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 (2dbfdf9c2d5defd09f7a, 5d530b2f228ed39ff952, ca467c94f14b2219503e). Premeasurement V2 errors switch from +13.95 to -37.64 mL across the outer ratios, identifying an overly compressed predicted response. By comparison, measured m16 and m76 responses are modest, with substantially smaller prospective errors.

Measured evidence retains heterogeneous ordinary responses: m38 rises from 9.32/20.87 at 5/1 to 31.48/58.15 at 20/1 (7b341f30a27433562690, 8f9a7ca0380c405ee685). The latter was underpredicted by 17.90/18.33 mL, almost a common displacement, while physical interval width was predicted closely. m128 rises from 12.16/20.42 at 2/1 to 33.49/73.97 at 20/1 (40d5f6dbba8de32e9852, 55200f8e501a16ffa0cf), with 20/1 errors of -16.79/-37.94: missing interval width accompanies early endpoint predictions. Conversely, m189 onset falls from 6.87 at 2/1 to 4.39 at 20/1 while completion rises from 14.97 to 23.10 (f1dafc187f7b1ec15297, fd9cda2d3ab32ea2a360), rejecting the transferred onset delay. These failures require different corrections.
ml_scientist.important_model_behaviors:
Current model diagnostic: loading sensitivity remains almost absent in many contrasts. At m128 5/1, 50 and 150 mg predict approximately 12.747/29.551 and 12.743/29.564 mL (cdcabd704ebeeeca9183, 91cd087e44e7a3364533). Similar near-invariance occurs across m28 1/1 doses. Flatness is appropriate for some measured comparisons; the concern is conditional sensitivity, illustrated by m211's different dose responses at 10/1 and 50/1.

Current quantile diagnostic: adbaa4b00d492d64eed5 has V1 q10/median/q90 approximately 3.81/4.14/3.44 and negative reported width. f180b04a7fd838088661 has positive width despite q90 below the median. m110 candidate 8f7bcdb92b0cd7acad94 has V1 q90 below its median and V2 q10 above its median. Width cannot be interpreted as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Refresh examples after retraining: f106b85660c480a44538 and 686562279e2bfb73ef1e now have ordered supplied quantiles, so their earlier crossing descriptions are obsolete.

Inference: maximum historical error conflates timing displacement, missing interval width and incorrect onset slope. Current adaptation around acquired labels is a fit diagnostic, not evidence of prospective transfer.
ml_scientist.possible_learning_bottlenecks:
Inference from this trajectory: corrections at acquired endpoints do not reliably identify intervening response functions. m13's opposite residual signs across ratios and m45's overpredicted interiors directly support this concern. Interior labels are valuable when they distinguish response amplitude or shape, rather than merely densifying an already resolved curve.

ML prior: examine condition scaling and interaction capacity before expecting extensive additional dose supervision to repair persistent feature insensitivity. Diagnose finite differences separately for V1 and V2 at fixed graph and eluent. Density times injection volume supplies mass here; density differences across graphs are not automatically causal chromatography effects.

ML prior: assess sensitivity against actual EA fraction, and potentially a transformed composition coordinate, alongside the supplied ratio. Equal increments in PE/EA ratio represent unequal changes in EA fraction. This can clarify apparent curvature without imposing universal endpoint monotonicity.
ml_scientist.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns:
The pool includes familiar graphs with informative unmeasured conditions and a clear remaining graph novelty, m202, whose maximum observed similarity is approximately 0.409. Similarity 1 does not establish solvent-curve coverage. m16, m38, m76, m149, m157 and m189 now have measurements; their earlier status as unmeasured exploration targets is obsolete.

Assess physical redundancy using molecule plus all five condition columns. Exact eligible duplicates include m54 50/1 IDs 533e50b0595be82d2716 and f7bbba9684bf7983ccbf. Candidate 41ae24734eabf9cae4d7 repeats the measured m76 input in 3fd8f569aaeff7edebea and would be replication. Tiny mass differences do not automatically add useful coverage.

Binary condition novelty and cw_distance_percentile do not estimate retraining benefit or Row density. Empty pending records make similarity-to-pending uninformative. Further broad m82, m27, m28-dose, m73, m80, m124, m173 or m194 programs have reduced immediate value unless a particular result would change interpretation.

ml_scientist.warnings:
Only observed-table records establish measured evidence. Candidate endpoints remain predictions, including candidates sharing measured physical inputs. Historical errors are premeasurement prediction minus measurement. Adaptive residuals do not estimate unbiased overall Row error or demonstrate retraining improvement.

Use actual loading_amount_mg and complete condition tuples. The m120 higher-loading 5/1 record uses 111.3 mg, not 166.95 mg. m195's 50/100 mg 20/1 candidates change dose relative to its unusual 150 mg record and cannot establish same-input reproducibility.

Preserve conflicting m73 records and m195's slightly reversed measured interval. m195's early measured onset at 2/1 and 10/1 leaves its abrupt 20/1 onset change unresolved; it does not identify the latter label as erroneous. Recurrence of broad m194 completion across conditions is not same-input reproducibility. V2 minus V1 is physical elution interval width, distinct from predictive quantile width. All conclusions use only this seed and method's supplied trajectory.
